evidence: Read every criterion description in all five judge.toml files (2 gates, 44 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual likert) and scanned each for the row-33 defect: a list of requirements followed by a waiver of most of them, which leaves the judge two full-credit targets. No instance found. Every binary criterion ends with the uniform conjunctive closer 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' Its explicit 'Fails if ...' list matches the positive conditions it enumerates. Each permissive clause narrows HOW a single bar may be evidenced and does not drop an enumerated requirement: (a) Where-shown alternatives. hro_reject_reason (functional/judge.toml:83) accepts the reason or rejected-from stage 'on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line' and fails only if they are 'not available to staff anywhere'. hro_job_open (:29) requires team/manager/places to be 'shown wherever the app shows job details or are evidenced by behaviour'. hro_add_candidate (:38) requires email/source 'wherever the app shows card details'. These are one 'if shown, correct' bar, and their fail lists say 'a shown value is wrong' / 'shows wrong details'. (b) Route alternatives. hro_move_one_stage (:56), hro_reject_hired (:92), hro_mgr_other_job (:164): 'whether tried through the UI or, if not offered, by replay; hiding it is optional'. The bar is still 'server refuses, card unchanged', which matches the prompt line 23 rule 'Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice'. (c) Scope exclusions. These name another row as owner without waiving anything inside the row: hro_arrive_bottom (:65) 'belongs to hro_bulk_move'; hro_interview_full (:110) 'belongs to hro_bulk_places ... hro_undo_full'; hro_undo_restores (:245) 'graded only in hro_undo_conflict'; hro_refusal_status (:200) 'Only the status is graded here'; hro_candidate_view (:389); hro_drafts (:380); hro_pol_live_thread and hro_pol_failed_send (polish/judge.toml:19,37). They agree with prompt line 19 ('deducted only in hro_activity_refusals') and line 23 ('Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'). (d) Explicit tolerances. Render gate 'a refusal message is welcome but not required'; constraints gate 'another working staff account is acceptable'; hro_activity 'one line naming every card of a multi-card move ... also satisfies'; hro_pol_failed_send 'a local not-sent marker is acceptable'; hro_pol_session_resume 'unless the sign-in prompt has already appeared on its own (that also passes)'; hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'. Each tolerance relaxes the form of one requirement and keeps the outcome. (e) Conditional leg. hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:10) drops the scroll leg only under a stated, checkable precondition ('only if neither can be made to scroll with twelve cards in one stage, record that and judge the other legs'), and its fail list still includes 'resets scroll'. That is one decision rule, not two targets. (f) The five visual likert rows each state one dimension with five ordered anchors (visual/judge.toml:4-76) and no waivers. Multi-leg rows such as hro_restart, hro_activity, hro_observer_readonly, hro_anonymous and hro_candidate_private bundle one flow into one conjunctive bar. The skill's Known false positives (SKILL.md: 'One criterion covering a whole flow ... (checks 26, 28, 33)') and the Internal Quality Checks annotation on row 33 classify that as a non-defect for this row; whether such bundles should be split for independent credit belongs to REVIEW_POLICY and other rows. app_context.md contains no waiver that contradicts a criterion. Adversarial attempts: (1) Broken app that might pass. An app that never displays a card's source or a job's team passes those 'wherever shown' legs in hro_add_candidate/hro_job_open. That is a deliberate single conditional bar, and team is still graded unconditionally in hro_candidate_view (:389, 'job title, team and status'). Whether source display is a public requirement is a coverage question for other rows, not a self-consistency defect. (2) Conforming app that might fail. An app whose board never scrolls even at 12 cards is protected by the explicit carve-out in hro_pol_live_board. An app that shows the rejection reason only in Activity is protected by hro_reject_reason's 'anywhere'. Neither the weak app nor the conforming app gets a second contradictory target. Minor observations, not defects: hro_candidate_no_staff (:182) states 'or the staff control did not succeed' explicitly, while hro_observer_readonly (:173) and hro_anonymous (:191) leave that consequence to prompt line 13 ('Every refusal row needs its own positive control'). The bar is the same, stated less explicitly in two places. Several fail lists sit before trailing sentences ('The entered source is shown ...', 'The Observer can read the same lines.'), but the closing catch-all covers them.
